newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN GRAIN HARVEST SPEEDS ALONG, RYE VARIABLE.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN GRAIN HARVEST SPEEDS ALONG, RYE VARIABLE.

text.p: Germany's barley and rye harvests are due to be mostly completed this week, aided by sunny weather, farm sources said on Monday.
Wheat harvesting was also expected to make good progress in the south and the west.

A source at Lower Saxony's agricultural chamber in Hanover said rye quality and yields varied widely. Falling numbers, which measure baking quality, were lower than hoped as a result of heavy rains in July.
The result might be a fall in prices and large sales of rye into intervention. Ergot occurrence was lower than in previous years and that at least qualified rye for intervention.
Some rye producing regions in eastern Germany reported only 30 to 50 percent of the rye had falling numbers above 120 seconds.
That represented the minimum for bread rye, although millers would buy lots with lower falling numbers at discounts.
Elsewhere in the east farmers had achieved falling numbers of 150-200, while other regions reported just under 120 (west), just above 120 (north) and mostly above 100 (south).
The total rye area was up four percent at 843,310 hectares and there should be no shortage of milling rye, traders said.
Rye yields so far had been around 8.00 tonnes per hectare in the west, 6.00-8.00 in the north, 6.5-7.0 in the south-west and less than 6.00 in the south.
Germany last year harvested 4.2 million tonnes of rye at an average yield of 5.21 tonnes per ha.
Traders said the newly harvested wheat had initially been expected to have a low protein content, but that had not happened on a large scale.
